title: Production model certification checklist — MCert v1.0
author: Priya Menon
content:
Overview

Purpose: This checklist defines the minimum evaluation, performance, safety, and operational requirements a model must meet before being certified for production serving on Redwood. It bundles artifacts, automated checks, and manual signoffs into a repeatable workflow (MCert). Use this document for new-model onboarding, major-version upgrades, and any model variant that will be used for live traffic.

Scope: applies to open and third-party models selected for Redwood-hosted or Dedicated serving. It covers functional evals, prompt sensitivity, quantization testing, perf benchmarking, observability instrumentation, rollout strategy, and rollback criteria.

Owners and signoff flow

- Model owner: individual or product engineer responsible for the model (create a PR with artifacts).
- Certifying authority: Applied ML team (final technical signoff).
- SRE owner: Eng-SRE (capacity and SLO validation).
- Security reviewer: Security & Compliance (privacy/KMS checks if required).
- Business stakeholder: Product/PoC owner (acceptance for business QA).

Signoff sequence (required): model owner -> applied-ml reviewer -> SRE -> security -> product. The Applied ML reviewer must attach a summary report and link to automated eval dashboards.

Required artifacts (deliverables)

1) Model Card (MD or Confluence link) — includes architecture, tokenizer, license, pretraining data summary, and known limitations.
2) Eval report bundle (ZIP) with:
   - deterministic eval run outputs: exact seed, prompt versions, temperature, and sampling settings used.
   - prompt-suite results: production prompt catalog subset + adversarial subsets.
   - per-prompt metrics: ROUGE/BLEU/ExactMatch where relevant and task-appropriate metrics.
3) Performance benchmark report (CSV + graphs):
   - latency distribution (p50, p95, p99) for sequences: 32, 128, 512, 2048 tokens.
   - throughput (tokens/sec) and max sustained qps for target GPU instance types.
   - memory (GPU RAM) footprint with KV-cache sizing.
4) Quantization profile artifact (if quantized) — settings, expected quality delta, and quant test logs.
5) Observability checklist: tracing spans instrumented, relevant metrics added to model-specific dashboard, log-levels, and error tagging semantics.
6) Safety / guardrail evidence: toxicity scores, hallucination checks, controlled-output examples, and mitigations.
7) Canary rollout plan: target segments, traffic weights, monitoring windows, rollback triggers.
8) Test harness config: eval-harness job spec (YAML) used to reproduce all checks.

Minimum automated checks (must pass)

- Functional correctness: unit tests and deterministic evals pass with no flaky failures in 5 repeated runs.
- Prompt stability: median semantic-drift <= 2% (task-dependent) across 10% perturbation of prompt templates.
- Quality regression: no more than 1.5% absolute drop on primary metric vs baseline (or explicit exception logged).
- Safety threshold: toxicity rate <= 0.5% on in-domain prompts; high-risk categories blocked by filter.
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency <= 350ms for 128-token requests on the certified instance family.
- Memory safety: max GPU memory < 90% on worst-case sequence workloads.

Quantization-specific tests

- End-to-end quality delta report: compare float32 baseline vs quantized variant on the accepted prompt-suite and adversarial set. Provide per-metric delta and confidence intervals.
- Per-workload perf uplift report: tokens/sec and latency improvements aggregated by sequence length.
- Stability stress test: run continuous inference for 4 hours with KV-cache warmup and validate no memory leaks or progressive drift in output quality.
- If expected quality delta > 2% for any primary metric, require either user-facing fallback or additional guardrails.

Performance benchmarking procedure (executable steps)

1) Provision test infra: use dedicated perf cluster (list in Confluence infra page) matching intended instance type.
2) Warmup: run 1k sample inference requests from production prompt sample to populate KV cache.
3) Run 3 independent benchmark passes for each sequence length (32/128/512/2048), each pass at 80% target concurrency.
4) Capture traces, GPU metrics (utilization, memory, SM clocks), and host metrics.
5) Generate consolidated report; annotate outliers and any system-level throttling.

Example CLI commands

- Trigger eval-harness job (local):
  ./eval-harness/run_local.sh --model-path=artifacts/model-v1 --prompts=prompts/production.json --out=reports/model-v1-evals.json

- Perf runner (k8s job):
  kubectl apply -f perf-jobs/model-v1-run.yaml --namespace=perf

- Quick quant check (internal tooling):
  rquant profile --model artifacts/model-v1 --backend cuda --bits 4 --out=artifacts/quants/model-v1-q4.json

Recommended SLOs and thresholds (suggested defaults)

| Metric | Suggested threshold | Notes |
|-------|--------------------:|------|
| p50 latency (128 tokens) | <= 120 ms | interactive targets |
| p95 latency (128 tokens) | <= 350 ms | hard SLO for hosted tiers |
| throughput (tokens/sec) | >= 40k | depends on instance class |
| memory headroom | >= 10% | to avoid OOM during bursts |
| quality regression vs baseline | <= 1.5% abs | primary task metric |

Rollout plan template (canary-first)

1) Canary 1 (1% traffic) — 30 minutes: auto-checks for errors, latencies, token cost, and eval metrics on sampled responses.
2) Canary 2 (5% traffic) — 2 hours: run longer stability checks including periodic adversarial prompts.
3) Ramp to 25% — 4 hours: monitor SLOs, error budget usage, and user-facing quality signals.
4) Full release to 100% — after 24h stable canary behavior.

Rollback triggers (any of the following triggers immediate rollback):

- Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute compared to baseline in observation window.
- p95 latency degradation > 1.5x relative to baseline.
- Quality regression on primary metric > 2.5% absolute.
- Evidence of new failure modes (security/privacy) discovered in logs.

Operational runbook snippets

- To force a rollback: use the rollout manager CLI:
  rdeploy rollback --model-id model-v1 --to-tag stable

- To collect debug bundle for Applied ML and SRE:
  rcollect bundle --model model-v1 --since 2026-02-14T10:00:00Z --out /tmp/model-v1-debug.tar.gz

- Typical queries to reproduce a user issue (example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"model-v1","input":"<failing prompt>"}'

Checklist (quick pass/fail list)

- [ ] Model card uploaded and reviewed
- [ ] Eval harness runs reproducible and attached
- [ ] Perf benchmarks meet target SLOs
- [ ] Quantization tests (if applied) completed and within delta limits
- [ ] Observability dashboard created and linked
- [ ] Canary plan documented with monitoring queries
- [ ] Security signoff (if required)
- [ ] Product acceptance for feature behavior
- [ ] Final Applied ML certification signoff

Appendix: Minimal eval-harness YAML example

pipeline: run
- name: load-prompts
  type: prompts
  source: s3://redwood-evals/prompts/production.json
- name: infer
  type: inference
  model: artifacts/model-v1
  sampling: {temperature: 0.0, top_p: 0.95}
- name: scoring
  type: metric
  metrics: [exact_match, bleu]

Notes and guidance

- If a model is borderline on a threshold, attach a mitigation plan (e.g., config to route sensitive prompts to float baseline).
- Keep the eval-harness job specs and quant artifacts immutable in the release bundle to guarantee reproducibility.
- For Dedicated customer deployments, ensure that the regional performance matrix is validated against the customer’s provisioned instance family.
